analyst_view.overall: Borac (21st, 3 pts) host Atalanta (16th, 4 pts) in a game both need for a top-24 place, and a win could lift Atalanta toward the top eight. Borac have won four of their last six in all competitions, are second in the Bosnian league and unbeaten at home in Europe this season, conceding once in four European home games; Cipetic is their only fitness check. Atalanta come off a 4-4 draw with Inter and are without keeper Carnesecchi (counted; Sportiello starts, with only teenagers behind him) and centre-backs Hien and Kossounou, while Kristensen and Gaetano are listed as doubtful. Sarri, who asked for 'courage and humility', is expected to rotate with Lecce away on Monday: Scamacca up front, Pasalic for Ederson and Kolasinac in defence, with reports split on whether De Ketelaere starts. Belgian referee Nathan Verboomen has no usable record in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, about 2 of them Atalanta's, already lifted for Borac's recent scoring and for Carnesecchi's absence (+6%). Hien and Kossounou have been out for weeks, so recent form carries that, while a rotated attack led by Scamacca instead of the first-choice front line pulls the other way, and Borac have been tight at home in Europe; those roughly cancel, so I stay at about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, about 6 for Atalanta, already raised for Borac conceding plenty of corners lately (+7% for Atalanta). A rotated Atalanta still plays wide with full-backs like Bellanova and Bernasconi, and Borac will defend deep for long spells, which is what the split already shows, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and already raise Borac's share about 19% for their recent bookings. A sold-out home crowd and a home side chasing a stronger team can mean more fouls, but that is what the numbers already show, and referee Verboomen has too little record at this level to point either way, so I stay at about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.1 shots, 19 of them Atalanta's, already lifted for both sides' recent volume. I lean slightly lower: after a draining 4-4 with Inter and with Lecce on Monday, Sarri is expected to rotate and may manage the game rather than chase it, and Borac have kept European visitors quiet at home, which the numbers can't see. A mild -3% gives about 31.1 shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target, already raised for both sides' recent accuracy. Sportiello in goal behind a makeshift centre-back pair points to chances for Borac, which the numbers partly count through Carnesecchi's absence, while a rotated Atalanta attack may be a little less sharp; those roughly cancel, so I stay at about 10.7.
